items.recapEn: In Yokkaichi, under the factory lights across the water, Hana and Ken ate ramen at Noguchi-san's counter beside Ryō, a night-shift worker on his evening off. Hana admitted the view was not exactly pretty; Ken said it had no lies in it. Tomorrow: tonteki. Ryō said the lights look best from the big bridge at two in the morning.

items.recapEn: On the bridge after dinner, Hana and Ken watched the complex across the bay: not pretty, though; honest, though. Ken saw a kitchen at night, every pot still warm. Hana counted two kindnesses, noted the old post town under the factory town, and rewrote her stiff first line in Ken's plain words. Two in the morning? Both asleep.
